original_question: For a field F and positive integer n, is the n-torsion subgroup nBr(F) generated by Brauer classes of cyclic algebras of degree dividing n?
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the right ambient objects (a field F and an integer n), the right Brauer-group piece (the n-torsion subgroup), and the right generating candidates (Brauer classes of cyclic algebras). That is essentially the exact open problem stated in the paper. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304v2.pdf))
missing_details: Make the quantifiers explicit: the paper asks this for every field F and every positive integer n, not for a fixed field or a fixed n. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304v2.pdf))
Use the paper’s notation {}_nBr(F) and define it stand-alone as the n-torsion subgroup of Br(F), i.e. {[A] in Br(F) : n[A] = 0}. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304v2.pdf))

State that the generators live inside Br(F): one is asking whether {}_nBr(F) is generated as a subgroup of the Brauer group by Brauer classes of cyclic central simple F-algebras. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304v2.pdf))

Unpack ‘cyclic’ if the question is to be fully stand-alone: in the paper’s background, a cyclic algebra is a central simple F-algebra containing a cyclic Galois maximal subfield over F. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304v2.pdf))

Keep the paper’s exact degree wording ‘degree (dividing) n’; your draft’s ‘degree dividing n’ is mathematically close, but the official formulation keeps the parenthetical. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304v2.pdf))
Do not weaken the question to the neighboring Problem 3.4, which asks only whether {}_nBr(F) is generated by algebras of degree n. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304v2.pdf))
refined_question: For every field F and every positive integer n, is the n-torsion subgroup {}_nBr(F) := {[A] in Br(F) : n[A] = 0} generated, as a subgroup of Br(F), by Brauer classes of cyclic central simple F-algebras of degree (dividing) n? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304v2.pdf))
justification: The draft is aiming at the general Albert question in §3, not at a different nearby problem. The paper first defines Br(F) and cyclic algebras in §0, then motivates the question in §3 via the Merkurjev–Suslin theorem and states Problem 3.1 in essentially the same words. The adjacent Problem 3.4 is explicitly weaker, so the refined version should stay with Problem 3.1 rather than drift to that variant. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304v2.pdf))
